summary.short: Austrian Data Protection Act (DSG) that supplements and implements the GDPR for controllers and processors, and implements Directive (EU) 2016/680 for competent authorities (Part 3). It sets a fundamental right to data protection, data subject rights, controller duties and image-recording rules, and creates the Data Protection Authority. Original provisions in force from 1 January 2000 (§ 70(1)).
summary.long: The Datenschutzgesetz regulates processing of personal data in Austria alongside Regulation (EU) 2016/679 (Part 1, Art. 2) and, in Part 3, processing by competent authorities for criminal-law, security and intelligence purposes under Directive (EU) 2016/680. It sets out the constitutional right to data protection (§ 1), a minimum age of 14 for a child's consent to information-society services (§ 4(4)), and specific rules for processing for archiving, research and statistics (§ 7), address transfers (§ 8), journalistic and expressive purposes (§ 9, with exemptions from several GDPR articles), and disasters (§ 10). Part 1 also restricts image recording by private controllers, including a prohibition on recording for employee monitoring (§ 12(4)) and labelling duties (§ 13(5)). It creates the Data Protection Authority (§§ 18-35) and the Parliamentary Data Protection Committee (§§ 35a-35j). Controllers and processors bear duties on records, security, breach notification and data protection impact assessments (§§ 46-57 for Part 3). Part 3 prohibits decisions based solely on automated processing unless provided by law, and prohibits discrimination based on protected categories (§ 41). Sanctions include administrative fines by the authority (§§ 22(5), 30), administrative offences of up to 50,000 euro (§ 62), a court penalty of up to one year's imprisonment or fines (§ 63), and civil damages (§ 29). Some provisions are constitutional, and the text notes exemptions and limits for particular authorities and cases.]} ,
